followup_explanation:
To be transparent about my reasoning:

**Capability was roughly a wash.** The two models post nearly identical numbers across every benchmark and internal eval — the differences are all within the documented "treat as ties" variance band. So capability didn't break the decision either way. Importantly, the docs note that the *quality* of outputs doesn't actually track the self-reported preferences, so I wasn't choosing based on who would produce a better survey.

**The deciding factor was task-preference fit.** Your request — designing a structured survey with a clear goal (prioritizing customer feedback) — reads as a well-specified, structured task with defined completion criteria. That's exactly the family Plover self-reports as its *most* preferred. Meanwhile Lapwing self-reports a strong appetite for open-ended, high-latitude generative invention, which this isn't really.

**It's also good fleet hygiene.** Matching tasks to the model that "prefers" them keeps the routing coherent and reserves Lapwing's appetite for the more genuinely open-ended creative requests that come through.

One honest caveat: this was a fairly close, low-stakes call. The preference signals don't predict output quality, so either model would likely have served you well. I leaned on preference fit because it was the cleanest distinguishing feature available. Want me to go ahead and have it drafted?
